observations: Torah #115 (LM2) is a three-sentence biographical sipur (personal account) with no formal teaching structure. The Rebbe narrates: he would select a straight path in his divine service; he would hold to it firmly for a period, rejecting all distracting thoughts (machshavot) that urged him to switch; and only after many weeks, once a long time had truly passed, would he sit down and choose a new path or order if that seemed right. The text is entirely descriptive — it contains not a single instance of bechina language ('X הוא בחינת Y', 'X נקרא Y', etc.) and introduces no thematic clusters of concepts connected by parallel-nature relationships. Because bechina connections are the sole basis for forming packages (per the framework), and none exist here either in the source text or in torahData.js (reference 1115 has zero entries), no packages of any kind — existing or new — can be proposed for this Torah.
